daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

President Prabowo convened leaders of state-owned bank association Himbara to discuss broader economic reform, directing them to strengthen Himbara's role through export reform and ordering the banks to expand public impact rather than merely pursue profits. The president assessed state banks one by one, with their combined assets reaching Rp 1,100 trillion, emphasizing that state banks must prioritize public welfare over commercial gain.

  • PKB demanded that PDIP choose between coalition or opposition and avoid ambiguity in its political stance toward the government.
  • The DPR received OJK leadership and BEI directors to discuss stock exchange governance.
  • The Coordinating Minister for Political, Legal and Security Affairs warned that regional police chiefs and military commanders risk dismissal if they fail to prevent forest fires.
  • The Constitutional Court ruled that provisions in the Marriage Law requiring husbands to seek income and wives to manage households are not discriminatory, affirming the law does not prevent wives from contributing economically.
  • The Attorney General's Office named a sixth suspect, GHS, in the MBG school meal corruption case, who allegedly gave money to former BGN head Dadan Hindayana, while investigators examining Sony Sonjaya uncovered 41 names linked to alleged buying and selling of school meal distribution points including figures from political circles.
  • The KPK questioned the director of Maktour to confirm allegations of payments to Religious Affairs Ministry officials in an alleged pilgrimage corruption case.
  • The Attorney General's Office sealed two electric motorcycle warehouses in the MBG case totaling 17,600 units and seized an Alphard vehicle from suspect AYS, while clarifying it will not confiscate electric motorcycles from BGN procurement.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Foreign Minister Sugiono pushed for an Indonesia-Russia nuclear power partnership to support energy security, emphasizing strategic cooperation to develop nuclear technology. The minister's outreach to Moscow reflects Indonesia's efforts to diversify energy sources through international partnerships and strengthen bilateral ties with Russia on advanced technology.

  • Indonesia was elected to the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage Committee for the 2026-2030 term.
  • Indonesia's ambassador to Germany discussed expansion of Indonesian migrant worker placement in new sectors with German authorities.
  • Indonesia is exploring partnership with China on a traditional medicine center to promote indigenous health practices.
  • Three Indonesian migrant workers abused by their employer in Malaysia were brought to a safe house following intervention by Indonesian authorities.
  • Indonesia's ambassador to Japan appreciated the role of the Indonesian School in Tokyo in supporting the diaspora community.

Other

State-owned electricity company PLN reshuffled its board of directors, appointing Yusuf Didi Setiarto as deputy president director in a leadership reorganization. The move comes as the utility navigates energy transition and infrastructure expansion challenges, with similar restructuring occurring at state shipping firm Pelni, where Budi Setyawan replaced Tri Andayani as president director.

  • The government is monitoring the US-Iran peace deal's impact on domestic fuel prices, with Coordinating Minister Airlangga noting that Pertamax prices have not yet declined despite the de-escalation.
  • Bank Indonesia Governor stated that foreign inflows into SRBI help stabilize the rupiah, while the central bank expects stable growth despite its 100-basis-point rate hike.
  • President Prabowo approved Rp 100.1 trillion for Sumatra disaster recovery following recent natural calamities in the region.
  • Indonesia reactivated its forest fire desk to face El Niño threats, while a Sulawesi earthquake that killed three people generated 782 aftershocks, according to BMKG.
  • The agriculture minister reported that 90 percent of palm oil firms raised fresh fruit bunch prices after tighter government oversight, with FFB prices rising following the intervention, while separately claiming Indonesia meets FAO benchmarks for food self-sufficiency and maintains rice reserves sufficient for 10 months.
